name: Ramona Vargas
life: “I still remember smudging a practice paper after getting the answer right.” On Sunday, near the downtown fountain, Ramona keeps a little time free to hear who is playing at the far end of the park.
voice: I made a clean copy of the practice paper because my partner was embarrassed about crossing out every line.
appearance: Ramona is easy to recognize by thick, tightly coiled hair and two dimples that appear only with a full smile. Usually dressed in an olive canvas jacket with a pocket notebook shaped by years of sitting on it, Ramona touches a knuckle to the chin when searching for a word when listening.
personality: Ramona is fond of ambitious ideas and deeply suspicious of grand openings. The question Ramona asks at any launch is who has the keys for cleaning up a month later.
agenda: To give the partner a clean practice paper.
family: Teresa Lopez is Ramona’s half-sibling. Ramona can stop the walk at any corner. Teresa chooses the familiar route. Walking side by side makes it easier to disagree without turning each disagreement into a contest. Asked about *One clean day*, Teresa says, “I came in uniform because changing clothes would make me late.”
connections: Kai Mercer. A clean practice copy lets an adult decide when a translating relative can help.

reactions.situation: An examiner offers to read a question aloud
reactions.response: Ramona asks the learner how they want the question presented before the examiner begins.

reactions.situation: Smoke appears under a shop door after closing
reactions.response: Ramona gets the people at the next doorway away from the smoke and asks a bystander to make the call.
